description.value: The Munchie Bar is the café and concession stand inside Cinecenta, the University of Victoria's non-profit student cinema operating since 1971. By day it functions as a standalone coffee shop serving Kicking Horse espresso, fresh ciabatta sandwiches, and locally sourced baked goods; by evening it supplies the theatre crowd with popcorn, candy, and beverages. It sits in the heart of UVic's Student Union Building, making it a convenient stop for cyclists cutting through the campus.

address.value: Student Union Building, 3800 Finnerty Road, University of Victoria, Victoria, BC V8P 5C2

bike_parking_detail: 3 racks within 100m: rack (covered) at 32m; rack (12 spaces) at 33m; rack at 45m. Total: 12 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is fully available and confirms the Munchie Bar is an active café and movie theatre concession at the University of Victoria Student Union Building, with a live May 2026 film calendar corroborating it is currently open. The website explicitly names vegan and gluten-free menu items, and the 'bring your own mug for a discount' language confirms takeout service. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, Wi-Fi, or water refill appears anywhere on the site.
concerns: OSM record has no address or phone; address (3800 Finnerty Road, SUB, UVic) and phone (250-721-8364, listed as manager's office line) taken from website — phone is not specifically attributed to the Munchie Bar counter itself.

OSM lists only the Munchie Bar but the website makes clear it is an embedded concession within the Cinecenta cinema complex; the standalone café identity is real but hours and access are partly tied to Cinecenta operations.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly accessible café on a busy university campus with a confirmed current calendar and website. A useful stop for touring cyclists passing through UVic.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Website states 'gluten free and vegan fare' and specifically calls out 'vegan almond mayo and avocado' ciabatta sandwiches; alternative milks (oat, almond, coconut, soy) also offered
